(Scch-18) Dated: This 4th day of January 2020 Present: Sri.Mahantesh S.Dargad B.Sc., LL.B.,(Spl) Iii Addl. Judge & Member, Mact Court Of Small Causes, Bengaluru. M.V.C.No.1035/2018 Petitioner Kumari Poonam,G., Daughter of Guruswamy, Aged about 4 years, Since the petitioner is a minor, Represented by his father and natural guardian, Shri Guruswamy, Son of Ganesh, Aged about 36 years, Residing at No.716, Kalanagar, 3rd Cross, Channapatna Town, Channapatna Taluk, Ramanagara Distict. (By Pleader Shri Devaraju B.K.) V/s Respondents 1. Shri Gajendra C.V., 2 Scch-18 Mvc 1035/2018 Son of Vishwanath, No.1503, Kota Varadaraja Temple, K.P. Road, Ramanagara Taluk, Ramanagara District. (By Pleader Shri B.V.Venkatesha) 2. The Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., No.20, East Wings, 5th Floor, Centenary Building, M.G. Road, Bengaluru-560 001. Venkataraju) J U D G M E N T
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the petition are as under: On 1.6.2016 at about 9.00 p.m. the petitioner was playing infront of her house at 3rd cross, T.K. Road, Kalanagar, Channapatna Town, at that time the driver of the car bearing No.KA-51-C-8214 had taken the car in a reverse direction with high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human lie and safety of others and dashed against the petitioner. Consequent to the terrific impact, the petitioner was fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body. Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Government hospital, Channapatna, wherein she took the first aid treatment, thereafter she was shifted to NIMHANS and then he was referred to Victoria hospital, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient. 3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy, aged about 4 years, student. On account of the injuries she could not attend the class. The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car. Therefore, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation. Contending the above facts, she prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost. 4. In response to the petition notice, the respondents have appeared before the court through their counsel, inspite of sufficient opportunities given to the respondent No.1 has not filed his written statement, so the written statement of respondent No.1 is taken as not filed. The respondent No.2 has filed its respective written statement. 5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under: The respondent No.2 in its written statement averred that, the claim petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts. Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied mandatory provisions u/s 134 and S.158 (6) of the MV Act. Further admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA-51-C-8214 and its validity. Further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the above said vehicle as on the date of accident. Further contended that accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the Kumari Poonam vs Shri Gajendra C.V on 4 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147021359/ 2 parents of the minor petitioner and they leave minor girl in the public place without taking any responsible and caution and abruptly left the minor child alone in the main road and she is suddenly cross because of their own negligence she sustained injuries and she is solely responsible for the accident. Further contended that Nissan Sunny car bearing No.KA-51-C- 8214 is not at all involved in the accident. As per the complaint, car bearing No.KA-52-C-8214 is involved in the accident and as per FIR registered against the car bearing No.KA-52-C-8214, but during the course of investigation learnt that said car is not having valid insurance and the vehicle records the owner of the car and the petitioner in collusion with the police falsely implanted the Nissan Sunny car bearing No.KA-51-C-8214. Further denied the age avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition. Contending the above facts, prays to dismiss the claim petition with cost. 6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed: 1. 7. In order to prove the case, the father of the petitioner has examined as PW1 and got marked the documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P10 and doctor is examined as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P131 & Ex.P12 and PSI of Channapatna Police Station is examined as PW3. 8. To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondent No.2 has examined its Legal Manager as RW1 and got marked the document at Ex.R1. 9.
